`innerText` returns the text as it is rendered. The browser has to compute styles and layout to answer, and text hidden by CSS is left out. `textContent` returns the text of every node under the element without any of that work.

The rule does not know types. It reports `.innerText` on any object, and `innerText` in destructuring.

`--fix` renames the property access. Destructuring is left to you.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```js
const title = heading.innerText;
status.innerText = "Saved";
const { innerText } = heading;
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const title = heading.textContent;
status.textContent = "Saved";
const { textContent } = heading;
```

## When not to use it

If you want what the user sees, with hidden elements left out and line breaks where `<br>` and blocks are, `innerText` is the right property.
